reuse.why: Builds on the existing getScheduledAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, and routes schedule-template, forecast and the API model through shared helpers.

duplication.why: The missing/number/range dispatch is still repeated at the two app.ts sites and in the preview, which call getRangedAmount/getWorstCaseAmount piecemeal instead of one resolving function.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, where the tree keeps schedule amount logic.

scope.why: Focused on schedule amount resolution plus the API field, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Three overlapping entry points (getRangedAmount, getWorstCaseAmount, getScheduledAmount with inverse+op) and callers that choose different ones, some without the op, make it unclear which one applies the full rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule plus computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keep their own null/number/range dispatch around getRangedAmount instead of calling getScheduledAmount/getWorstCaseAmount with the op; api-models calls getScheduledAmount without the op

disguised_duplication.where: The amount == null ? 0 : number ? ... : range dispatch stays copied at app.ts (x2) and the preview, now split across getRangedAmount and getWorstCaseAmount calls

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter after inverse; getWorstCaseAmount has an isapprox branch; app.ts (2 sites) and the preview call getRangedAmount directly, api-models omits op
